questions.question: Present the Statement of Comprehensive Income of Molefe and de Waal Traders for the year ended 28 February, from sales to net profit, and explain why partners' salaries do not appear in it.
questions.expected_answer: Sales R2 460 000 less cost of sales R1 640 000 gives gross profit of R820 000. Add other operating income — rent income R38 400 and commission income R21 600, R60 000 — for gross operating income of R880 000. Less operating expenses of R441 000: salaries and wages R248 000, depreciation R54 400, trading stock deficit R2 100, bank charges R9 800, insurance R21 300, telephone R18 900, provision for bad debts adjustment R400, bad debts R6 100 and sundry expenses R80 000. Operating profit R439 000, less interest expense of R18 000 capitalised on the loan, gives net profit for the year of R421 000. Partners' salaries, interest on capital and the bonus are appropriations — the owners dividing profit among themselves after it is measured — so they appear in the current accounts note, never as expenses; expenses pay outsiders, appropriations sort out insiders. The heading reads FOR the year ended, because the statement covers a period.

questions.question: Assemble the Statement of Financial Position on 28 February in its two towers and show that they balance.
questions.expected_answer: Assets: non-current — fixed assets at carrying value R620 000, detailed in the note. Current assets R375 550: inventories R185 200; trade and other receivables — debtors R56 000 less the R2 800 provision giving R53 200, plus prepaid expenses R2 400 and accrued income R1 500; cash and cash equivalents — bank R131 050 and cash float R2 200. Total assets R995 550. Equity and liabilities: owners' equity R765 800 — capital accounts R700 000 plus current accounts R65 800; non-current liabilities — the loan at its closing balance of R138 000, capitalised interest included; current liabilities R91 750 — creditors R86 700, accrued expenses R1 850 and income received in advance R3 200. Total equity and liabilities R995 550, equal to total assets — the accounting equation published. Classification follows the twelve-month test, and debtors and fixed assets are shown net, with workings in the notes.

questions.question: Reconstruct the fixed assets note and the current accounts note, and show how each meets its figure on the face of the statement.
questions.expected_answer: Fixed assets note: land and buildings at R480 000 with no depreciation, since land does not wear out. Vehicles: cost R240 000, accumulated depreciation R109 600 at the start, depreciation for the year R48 000 at 20 percent on cost, closing accumulated depreciation R157 600, carrying value R82 400. Equipment: cost R120 000, accumulated depreciation R56 000 at the start, depreciation R6 400 at 10 percent diminishing balance, closing carrying value R57 600. The carrying values add to R620 000 — the face figure. The note also states the depreciation policy, as consistency requires. Current accounts note, per partner: opening balances R8 200 for Molefe and minus R5 400 for de Waal; interest on capital R36 000 and R27 000; salaries R120 000 and R144 000; bonus nil and R10 000; profit shares R48 000 and R36 000; drawings minus R176 000 and minus R182 000; closing balances R36 200 and R29 600, together R65 800 — the current accounts line inside equity on the face.
